analysis:
The supplied changes are test-only: EngineV2BridgeTests.swift and NativeBlockRetirementBridgeTests.swift under provider-swift/Tests. File-change excerpts show a decodeTable in the tokenizer stub, a stopStringScope parameter on the makeBridge helper, tests for scoped stop-sequence reporting (EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence), a native-block TextSession stub, and a test that native-block requests carry no stop scope. The head_text units I examined are unchanged surrounding tests: shared-KV budget accounting, SSD prefix-cache staging, lookup receipts, seeded request ids, and paged KV.

I saw no production code change, so there is no new attack surface or weakened control. The tests exercise existing mitigations in T-041 (SSD prefix cache, per-scope cacheSalt, KEK-keyed HMAC lookup tags, budget release on all paths). They create temp directories and use scripted memory snapshots, with no real secrets or network access.

Limits: the patch excerpts are truncated, and the production EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence and native-block stop-scope logic changes, if any, are outside this batch. A later pass should check that dropping the reasoning stop scope for native block requests does not alter the stop-string semantics consumers rely on. That is a correctness concern, not a security one, and I have no evidence of a regression.
